one_liner: Single-header C BC1-BC7 block decoder; 1.3-11x DirectXTex's single-thread throughput in aras-p's 2022 decoder comparison.
what_it_does: bcdec decodes one 4x4 block of any BCn (DXT/S3TC, RGTC, BPTC) format per call: bcdec_bc1 through bcdec_bc5, bcdec_bc6h_float or bcdec_bc6h_half, and bcdec_bc7. Each call takes a pointer to the compressed block, a destination pointer and a row pitch. You loop over blocks yourself, and nothing is allocated, loaded or parsed (no DDS reader, no image API). BC1/2/3/7 output RGBA8, BC4/BC5 output R8/RG8 (or float and signed with BCDEC_BC4BC5_PRECISE), and BC6H outputs RGB float32 or half. It is not an API drop-in for DirectXTex: DirectXTex's D3DXDecodeBCn returns 16 XMVECTOR floats per block, and its Decompress works on whole ScratchImages.
how_it_is_fast: It is plain scalar C with no SIMD. The speed comes from doing the work at word level instead of byte level (aras-p's PR #1): each block is loaded as 16/32/64-bit little-endian words, BC1 builds a 4-entry 32-bit RGBA palette and writes each pixel with one 32-bit store, and BC4/BC5 alpha indices are pulled from a 64-bit word 3 bits at a time. BC6H and BC7 use a two-word (128-bit) bitstream reader instead of per-bit extraction, plus hard-coded partition and fix-up tables. BC6H endpoint unquantization was moved out of the per-pixel loop (PR #8). BC1 palette interpolation uses multiply-shift 'magic' constants on the 5/6-bit endpoints instead of division (issue #15). DirectXTex, by contrast, decodes every texel through float XMVECTOR math and then packs back to 8-bit.
when_to_use: CPU-side decoding of BCn textures (asset pipelines, texture viewers, compression-quality evaluation, software fallbacks for GPUs without BCn support) where you want every format, including BC6H signed and unsigned, from one 1,500-line header.

Replacing DirectXTex's decoders outside Windows: no DirectXMath, DirectX-Headers or sal.h stubs needed, and it ran 4.85-11.4x faster on BC1 and 1.3-1.6x faster on BC7 in the 2022 single-thread comparison.
Embedding in C or C++ projects with strict dependency or licence rules: one header, no runtime library calls, MIT or Unlicense.
Multi-threaded decoding where you split the image into block ranges yourself: the functions keep no state between calls.
when_not_to_use: BC7-heavy workloads where decode speed matters: bc7enc_rdo's bc7decomp was 2.3-4.4x faster than bcdec on BC7 in the same 2022 charts (517 vs 220 Mpix/s on M1 Max, 621 vs 142 on a 5950X with VS2022).
Maximum BC1/BC3 throughput: etcpak's decoder was 1.16-1.7x faster on BC1 and BC3 in the same charts. It is harder to extract, though.

BC6H on Apple Silicon: in the 2022 M1 Max chart, bcdec (79 Mpix/s) trailed ConvectionKernels (149), SwiftShader (143) and Mesa (84). PR #8 (Sep 2022) sped BC6H up after those charts, and that change was not re-measured.

When you need bit-exact agreement with an older bcdec build or with a float reference. BC1 interpolation was off by up to 1 per channel until the June 2024 fix (issue #15). BC3/BC4/BC5 alpha rounding was changed in November 2024 (issue #12): BC3 alpha now truncates, and float-matching rounding needs BCDEC_BC4BC5_PRECISE.
Big-endian hosts, or when you need whole-image or DDS handling: the output stores pack 0xAABBGGRR as native 32-bit words, and edge blocks and padding are the caller's job.

integration.form: header-only (stb style: define BCDEC_IMPLEMENTATION in one translation unit; BCDEC_STATIC or BCDECDEF control linkage)
integration.min_toolchain: C with 64-bit unsigned long long (C99 or C++11 era compilers); built by MSVC 2022, clang 13/14 and GCC in the public harnesses
integration.platforms: any little-endian target; scalar code, no SIMD or intrinsics; since 2026-09-02 input blocks may be unaligned
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Functions keep no state; the static tables (partition sets, weights) are only read, so concurrent calls on different blocks are safe in practice.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same per-block job as DirectXTex's D3DXDecodeBC1..BC7, but different signatures (raw bytes out with a row pitch instead of 16 XMVECTOR floats), so call sites need small rewrites

gotchas: Pitch units differ by function: bytes for the 8-bit formats, but float or half elements for bcdec_bc6h_float and bcdec_bc6h_half (and for the BC4/BC5 float variants). The bcn_decoder_tester call passes width * 3 for BC6H float.

BCDEC_*_COMPRESSED_SIZE(w, h) computes (w>>2)*(h>>2) blocks, so it returns 0 for a 256x1 image and undercounts any size that is not a multiple of 4. Round dimensions up yourself. Issues #7 (tiny images) and #18 (256x1 BC3 crash) were in this area.

Output pixels are written through unsigned int, unsigned short and float pointers, so destination rows should be naturally aligned. Unaligned input reads were only fixed on 2026-09-02 (commit 80859ed, prompted by PR #23): DX10-header DDS payloads start at byte 148 and are never 8-byte aligned. Older copies are formally undefined behaviour there and fault on strict-alignment CPUs.
The maintainer rejects LLM-generated contributions (README; PR #23 was declined for that reason), so plan to carry local patches yourself if needed.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued image-codecs siblings (ffpng, fpng, QOI, libspng and others) decodes GPU block formats. Among block-texture entries, pick bcdec over etcpak or bc7enc_rdo's decoders when you want every BCn format, including BC2, BC4/BC5 signed and BC6H, in one header, and use those two only for peak BC1/BC3 (etcpak) or BC7 (bc7decomp) speed.
verified_claims_summary: aras-p's 'Comparing BCn texture decoders' (2022-06-23) is a third-party, single-threaded Mpix/s comparison; the post's source and chart PNGs are readable in the public aras-p/aras-p.hugo repo. The harness is public (aras-p/bcn_decoder_tester: 20 runs per DDS file, pinned submodules, test_images in the repo; Windows preset RelWithDebInfo plus /Ob2 with cl or clang-cl). Against DirectXTex (679538e), bcdec (e3ca0) measured BC1 1319 vs 272 (4.85x), BC3 704 vs 254 (2.77x), BC6H unsigned 85 vs 25 (3.40x) and BC7 142 vs 93 (1.53x) on a Ryzen 9 5950X with VS2022. With clang 14 on the same CPU: BC1 1449 vs 223 (6.50x), BC3 621 vs 207 (3.00x), BC7 169 vs 127 (1.33x). On an M1 Max with clang 13: BC1 2088 vs 183 (11.4x), BC3 1093 vs 185 (5.91x), BC7 220 vs 140 (1.57x). All ratios are derived from page data. Two caveats: the harness only warns on output-hash mismatch, and the measured bcdec had small rounding differences (BC1 off by up to 1 per channel; alpha bias +1) that were fixed in 2024 with integer operations of the same cost. The Mac build flags are not given in the presets.
status_note: Active (last commit 2026-09-02, alignment fix); single-header and MIT OR Unlicense, so it is trivially vendorable. Pin a version, because decoded values changed slightly in the 2024 rounding fixes.
